# DKR-012: No container mounts a sensitive host path

- **Group:** Docker
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

A bind mount of /, /etc, /root, /home, /proc or /sys hands the container the host's users, keys, credentials or kernel interfaces. Writable, a compromised container can add a user or an SSH key and own the host; read only, it can still read every secret there. A container that is not running (a one shot init container that exited, or a stopped one) is reported as info, since the setting matters only when it starts. The platform's own containers (Coolify's panel stack, coolify-proxy and coolify-sentinel; Dokploy's panel, database, Redis and Traefik) keep their findings at most at warn while the platform is detected, marked as managed by the platform, because the panel does not let you change them; privileged stays a fail.

## Verify by hand

```sh
docker inspect --format '{{.Name}} {{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}}:{{.Destination}}:{{.RW}} {{end}}' $(docker ps -aq)
```

## How to fix it

Mount only the specific files the container needs, read only (for example /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro), or use a named volume.

## What a fix can break

Containers that read or manage host files through the mount (backup agents, monitoring) lose that access.
